result.rationale: The diff verifiably shows the new addMembers/removeMember methods calling self.findMembers() inside .then with no rejection handler, and the controller actions (addMembers, removeMember) not using the returned promises at all (e.g. `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` with no .then/.fail). So failures in these new AJAX chains produce no user feedback — a real error-handling defect in newly introduced code, though severity is moderate since it manifests only on failures.

judged_text: removeMember and addMembers invoke `self.findMembers()` inside their `.then` without returning it and with no rejection handler, while the controller actions (admin-group.js.es6:56, 64) drop the returned promises entirely. The outer promise resolves success before the member list reload even starts, and when any link in the chain fails (a 4xx on add/remove, an expired session, a failed reload) the rejection is swallowed with no handler anywhere — the admin receives zero feedback and the member list silently shows stale state.
